ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $O$ lies on line $DE$, $\angle COD = 60^\circ$, $\angle BOD = \frac{1}{2}\angle COB$, and $OC$ is the bisector of $\angle AOB$. Find the degree measure of $\angle AOE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \text{Solution:} \quad \because \angle COD = 60^{\circ} = \angle DOB + \angle BOC, \]
\[ \therefore \angle DOB = 20^{\circ}, \, \angle BOC = 40^{\circ}, \]
\[ \because OC \text{ is the bisector of } \angle AOB, \]
\[ \therefore \angle AOB = 2\angle BOC = 80^{\circ}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle AOD = \angle DOB + \angle AOB = 100^{\circ}, \]
\[ \because D, O, E \text{ are collinear}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle DOE = 180^{\circ}, \]
\[ \therefore \angle AOE = \angle DOE - \angle AOD = 180^{\circ} - 100^{\circ} = \boxed{80^{\circ}}. \]
